metric:closed-tropical-rect.title: Container Preparation
metric:closed-tropical-rect.instruction: Clean the container with warm water first. If necessary, clean with a small amount of dish soap and thoroughly rinse. Ensure it is fully dry before starting.

metric:closed-tropical-rect.title: Drainage Layer
metric:closed-tropical-rect.instruction: Add 2-3cm of pebbles or [[leca|LECA]] to the bottom of your container.

metric:closed-tropical-rect.title: Separation Layer
metric:closed-tropical-rect.instruction: It's important that the [[drainage-layer|drainage layer]] be separate from the substrate. Most hobbyists opt for a fine mesh like a window screen, but you can also use a layer of [[sphagnum|sphagnum moss]].

metric:closed-tropical-rect.title: Substrate Layer
metric:closed-tropical-rect.instruction: Add 6-8cm of a standard well-draining terrarium mix. Press down on the mix gently to flatten, but try not to over compact.

metric:closed-tropical-rect.title: Plant Placement
metric:closed-tropical-rect.instruction: Plant the tallest or deepest-rooted plants first so that you can work around them: Pinstripe Calathea, Maidenhair Fern, Nerve Plant, Flame Violet.

metric:closed-tropical-rect.title: Initial Watering
metric:closed-tropical-rect.instruction: Based on these plants' needs, make sure your substrate is thoroughly wetted.

metric:closed-tropical-rect.title: Sealing / Ventilation Setup
metric:closed-tropical-rect.instruction: The building process can be stressful for plants. Seal the container completely and place in indirect light for 48 hours to stabilise.

metric:closed-tropical-rect.title: Your First Two Weeks
metric:closed-tropical-rect.instruction: The first two weeks decide whether your terrarium takes. First 48 hours: keep it in indirect light and let it stabilise — if the glass fogs up so heavily you can't see in, crack the lid for a few hours to let it clear, and watch it doesn't overheat in any sun. A little wilting now is normal transplant shock, not a watering cue. Days 2–14: check daily for mould or walls that stay fogged solid, and resist adding water — a sealed build is still finding its balance and almost always has enough. Once condensation clears by midday on its own, you can close it up and let the cycle run.

metric:open-arid-cyl.title: Separation Layer

metric:open-arid-cyl.title: Substrate Layer

metric:open-arid-cyl.title: Plant Placement
metric:open-arid-cyl.instruction: Plant the tallest or deepest-rooted plants first so that you can work around them: Mini Jade Plant, Zebra Haworthia, Mexican Snowball.

metric:open-arid-cyl.title: Initial Watering
metric:open-arid-cyl.instruction: Based on these plants' needs, give the terrarium a gentle misting.

metric:open-arid-cyl.title: Sealing / Ventilation Setup
metric:open-arid-cyl.instruction: No sealing needed. Monitor [[humidity]] closely during the first week.

metric:open-arid-cyl.title: Light Placement
metric:open-arid-cyl.instruction: Direct and bright-indirect light requirements conflict. Place in [[bright-indirect|bright indirect light]] to not scorch sun-sensitive plants. Plants that need higher light requirements may not survive.

metric:open-arid-cyl.title: Your First Two Weeks
metric:open-arid-cyl.instruction: The first two weeks decide whether your terrarium takes. Keep it in bright, indirect light and let the plants settle — a little wilting at first is normal transplant shock, not a watering cue. Over the next fortnight, check daily that the substrate stays evenly moist (an open build dries far faster than a closed one) and watch new growth for signs the light or [[humidity]] needs nudging. Mist if the foliage looks dry between waterings.

imperial:crowded.title: Drainage Layer
imperial:crowded.instruction: Add 0.8–1.2 in of pebbles or [[leca|LECA]] to the bottom of your container.

imperial:crowded.title: Separation Layer
imperial:crowded.instruction: It's important that the [[drainage-layer|drainage layer]] be separate from the substrate. Most hobbyists opt for a fine mesh like a window screen, but you can also use a layer of [[sphagnum|sphagnum moss]].

imperial:crowded.title: Substrate Layer
imperial:crowded.instruction: Add 2.4–3.1 in of a standard well-draining terrarium mix. Press down on the mix gently to flatten, but try not to over compact.

imperial:crowded.title: Plant Placement
imperial:crowded.instruction: Plant the tallest or deepest-rooted plants first so that you can work around them: Polka Dot Plant, Pinstripe Calathea, Friendship Plant, Nerve Plant, Flame Violet, Baby Tears.  Note: Baby Tears, Polka Dot Plant grow fast, so leave extra room around them.

imperial:crowded.title: Initial Watering
imperial:crowded.instruction: Based on these plants' needs, make sure your substrate is thoroughly wetted.

imperial:crowded.title: Sealing / Ventilation Setup
imperial:crowded.instruction: The building process can be stressful for plants. Seal the container completely and place in indirect light for 48 hours to stabilise.

imperial:crowded.title: Your First Two Weeks
imperial:crowded.instruction: The first two weeks decide whether your terrarium takes. First 48 hours: keep it in indirect light and let it stabilise — if the glass fogs up so heavily you can't see in, crack the lid for a few hours to let it clear, and watch it doesn't overheat in any sun. A little wilting now is normal transplant shock, not a watering cue. Days 2–14: check daily for mould or walls that stay fogged solid, and resist adding water — a sealed build is still finding its balance and almost always has enough. Once condensation clears by midday on its own, you can close it up and let the cycle run.

metric:sparse-fields.title: Container Preparation
metric:sparse-fields.instruction: Clean the container with warm water first. If necessary, clean with a small amount of dish soap and thoroughly rinse. Ensure it is fully dry before starting.

metric:sparse-fields.title: Drainage Layer
metric:sparse-fields.instruction: Add 1cm of pebbles or [[leca|LECA]] to the bottom of your container.

metric:sparse-fields.title: Separation Layer
metric:sparse-fields.instruction: It's important that the [[drainage-layer|drainage layer]] be separate from the substrate. Most hobbyists opt for a fine mesh like a window screen, but you can also use a layer of [[sphagnum|sphagnum moss]].

metric:sparse-fields.title: Substrate Layer
metric:sparse-fields.instruction: Add 3-5cm of a standard well-draining terrarium mix. Press down on the mix gently to flatten, but try not to over compact.

metric:sparse-fields.title: Plant Placement
metric:sparse-fields.instruction: Plant the tallest or deepest-rooted plants first so that you can work around them: Zebra Haworthia, Air Plant.

metric:sparse-fields.title: Initial Watering
metric:sparse-fields.instruction: Based on these plants' needs, give the terrarium a gentle misting.

metric:sparse-fields.title: Sealing / Ventilation Setup
metric:sparse-fields.instruction: No sealing needed. Monitor [[humidity]] closely during the first week.

metric:sparse-fields.title: Your First Two Weeks
metric:sparse-fields.instruction: The first two weeks decide whether your terrarium takes. Keep it in bright, indirect light and let the plants settle — a little wilting at first is normal transplant shock, not a watering cue. Over the next fortnight, check daily that the substrate stays evenly moist (an open build dries far faster than a closed one) and watch new growth for signs the light or [[humidity]] needs nudging. Mist if the foliage looks dry between waterings.

metric:full-fat-export-build.title: Container Preparation
metric:full-fat-export-build.instruction: Clean the container with warm water first. If necessary, clean with a small amount of dish soap and thoroughly rinse. Ensure it is fully dry before starting.

metric:full-fat-export-build.title: Drainage Layer
metric:full-fat-export-build.instruction: Add 2 cm of pebbles or [[leca|LECA]] to the bottom of your container.

metric:full-fat-export-build.title: Separation Layer
metric:full-fat-export-build.instruction: It's important that the [[drainage-layer|drainage layer]] be separate from the substrate. Most hobbyists opt for a fine mesh like a window screen, but you can also use a layer of [[sphagnum|sphagnum moss]].

metric:full-fat-export-build.title: Charcoal Layer
metric:full-fat-export-build.instruction: Add 1.5 cm of [[horticultural-charcoal|horticultural charcoal]] over the separation layer. Charcoal traps impurities and keeps the water cycle fresh. This is especially important if you are not using rain or distilled water.

metric:full-fat-export-build.title: Substrate Layer
metric:full-fat-export-build.instruction: Add 6 cm of your custom mix: 2 parts coco coir, 1 part perlite, 1 part sphagnum moss — a moisture-retentive, airy blend. Press down on the blend gently to flatten, but try not to over compact.

metric:full-fat-export-build.title: Plant Placement
metric:full-fat-export-build.instruction: Plant the tallest or deepest-rooted plants first so that you can work around them: Pinstripe Calathea, Maidenhair Fern, Nerve Plant.

metric:full-fat-export-build.title: Initial Watering

metric:full-fat-export-build.title: Sealing / Ventilation Setup
metric:full-fat-export-build.instruction: The building process can be stressful for plants. Close the lid, but crack it open briefly each day for the first week to allow gas exchange.
